title: Compiling and forecasting implied volatility surfaces via survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability sequence learning, and causal activity clocks
abstract: arXiv:2610.33438v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Compiling implied volatility (IV) surfaces and forecasting derivative risk from high-frequency equity and options feeds requires addressing contract heterogeneity, schema shifts, volatility clustering, and non-stationary trading activity. Using a split-adjusted NVIDIA (NVDA) equity and options panel (2018-2025), this study integrates finite-population survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability sequence learning, and causal activity clocks. Four findings emerge. First, cross-sectional surface accuracy depends on matching the sampling design to the target functional: plug-in stratified allocations using lagged cell dispersion improve equal-weighted surface reconstruction with full grid coverage, whereas liquidity-weighted probability proportional to size (PPS) sampling excels on liquidity-weighted targets by construction yet inflates error when misapplied. tldr: 论文将有限总体抽样设计、缓和逆概率加权序列学习与因果活动时钟相结合，利用NVDA 2018–2025年高频股票-期权数据编制并预测隐含波动率曲面，并发现横截面曲面精度关键在于使抽样设计与目标泛函相匹配。
en_tdlr: The paper integrates finite-population survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability-weighted sequence learning, and causal activity clocks to compile and forecast implied volatility surfaces from high-frequency NVDA equity-options data, showing that cross-sectional surface accuracy hinges on matching the sampling design to the target functional.
